elements.name: Arcane Archer (UA)
elements.desc: An Arcane Archer studies a unique elven method of archery that weaves magic into attacks to produce supernatural effects. Among elves, Arcane Archers are some of their most elite warriors. These archers stand watch over the fringes of elven domains, keeping a keen eye out for trespassers and using magic-infused arrows to defeat monsters and invaders before they can reach elven settlements. Over the centuries, the methods of these elf archers have been learned by members of other races who can also balance arcane aptitude with archery.

elements.name: Arcane Archer Revised (UA)
elements.desc: An Arcane Archer studies a unique elven method of archery that weaves magic into attacks to produce supernatural effects. Among elves, Arcane Archers are some of their most elite warriors. These archers stand watch over the fringes of elven domains, keeping a keen eye out for trespassers and using magic-infused arrows to defeat monsters and invaders before they can reach elven settlements. Over the centuries, the methods of these elf archers have been learned by members of other races who can also balance arcane aptitude with archery.

elements.name: Brute (UA)
elements.desc: Brutes are simple warriors who rely on mighty attacks and their own durability to overcome their enemies. Some brutes combine this physical might with tactical cunning. Others just hit things until those things stop hitting back.

elements.name: Cavalier (UA)
elements.desc: The archetypal Cavalier excels at mounted combat. Usually born among the nobility and raised at court, a Cavalier is equally at home leading a cavalry charge or exchanging repartee at a state dinner. Cavaliers also learn how to guard those in their charge from harm, often serving as the protectors of their superiors and of the weak. Drawn to right wrongs or earn prestige, many of these fighters leave their lives of comfort to embark on glorious adventure.

elements.name: Knight (UA)
elements.desc: The Knight is a colossus on the battlefield who can shrug off attacks and protect allies from harm. Knights fight from the saddle when they can, and in combat they are expected to seek out and lock down the mightiest of the enemy’s forces. On adventures, they are the armored bulwark that strives to keep the rest of the party safe.

rules.grant: Class Feature:Born to the Saddle (Knight UA)

elements.name: Monster Hunter (UA)
elements.desc: As an archetypal Monster Hunter, you are an expert at defeating supernatural threats. Typically mentored by an older, experienced Monster Hunter, you learn to overcome a variety of unnatural defenses and attacks, including those of undead, lycanthropes, and other creatures of horror.

rules.grant: Class Feature:Improved Combat Superiority (Monster Hunter UA)

elements.name: Psi Knight (UA)
elements.desc: Awake to the psionic power within, a Psi Knight is a fighter who augments their physical might with psi-infused weapon strikes, telekinetic lashes, and barriers of mental force. Many githyanki train to become such knights, as do some of the most disciplined high elves. In the world of Athas, renowned gladiators in the arenas of the Sorcerer-Kings are often Psi Knights, and in Eberron, the psionic kalashtar view membership in this knighthood as a special honor.

elements.name: Psychic Warrior (UA)
elements.desc: Awakening to the psionic power within themselves, a Psychic Warrior is a fighter who augments their physical might with psychically infused weapon strikes, telekinetic lashes, and barriers of mental force.

elements.name: Rune Knight (UA)
elements.desc: You discovered how to enhance your martial prowess using the supernatural power of runes. The ancient practice of rune magic originated with giants. Skiltgravr (“rune cutters”) can be found among any type of giants, and you likely learned your methods first or second hand from such a mystical artisan. Whether you found the giant’s work carved into a hill or cave, learned of the runes from a traveling sage, or met the giant in person, you studied the giant’s craft.

rules.grant: Class Feature:Blessing of the All Father (UA)

elements.name: Samurai (UA)
elements.desc: The Samurai is a fighter who draws on an implacable fighting spirit to overcome enemies. A Samurai's willpower is nearly unbreakable, and the enemies in a samurai's path have two choices: yield or die fighting.

elements.name: Scout (UA)
elements.desc: The archetypal scout excels at finding safe passage through dangerous regions. Scouts usually favor light armor and ranged weapons, but they are comfortable using heavier gear when faced with intense fighting.

elements.name: Sharpshooter (UA)
elements.desc: The Sharpshooter is a master of ranged combat. An excellent sniper and eagle-eyed scout, this fighter is a perilous foe who can defeat an entire war band so long as they are kept at range.

elements.name: Arcane Arrow (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Arcane Archer feature.

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn to channel magic into your attacks with a longbow or shortbow. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Archer's Lore (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Arcane Archer feature.

At 3rd level, you learn a few skills relating to the typical duties of an Arcane Archer. You learn to understand magical theory and develop survival skills for wandering the wilds. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Conjure Arrows (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Arcane Archer feature.

At 7th level, you learn a minor but useful magical trick. As an action, you can conjure 20 non-magical arrows. The arrows appear in your hand or in a container, such as a quiver, on your body. The arrows remain for 10 minutes or until you use this feature again; they then vanish.

elements.name: Ever-Ready Arrow (UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Arcane Archer feature.

Starting at 15th level, you can conjure forth a magic-infused arrow more often than before. One minute after expending your last remaining use of Arcane Arrow, you regain one use of it.

elements.name: Deadly Arrow (UA)
elements.desc:
18th-level Arcane Archer feature.

At 18th level, your Arcane Arrow's bonus damage increases to 4d6 force damage.

elements.name: Magic Arrow (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Arcane Archer Revised feature.

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to infuse arrows with magic. Whenever you fire a nonmagical arrow from a shortbow or longbow, you can make it a magic arrow, with a +1 bonus to the attack and damage rolls. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Arcane Shot (Revised UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Arcane Archer Revised feature.

At 3rd level, you learn to unleash special magical effects with some of your shots. When you gain this feature, you learn two Arcane Shot options of your choice (see the "Arcane Shot Options" section below). See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Arcane Archer's Lore (Revised UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Arcane Archer Revised feature.

At 3rd level, you learn magical theory or some of the secrets of nature—typical for practitioners of this elven martial tradition. You gain proficiency in either the Arcana or the Nature skill.

elements.name: Curving Shot (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Arcane Archer Revised feature.

At 7th level, you learn how to direct an errant arrow toward a new target. When you make an attack roll with a magic arrow and miss, you can use a bonus action to reroll the attack roll against a different target within 60 feet of the original target.

elements.name: Ever-Ready Shot (UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Arcane Archer Revised feature.

Starting at 15th level, your magical archery is ever available to you when you need it most. If you roll initiative and have no uses of Arcane Shot remaining, you regain one use of it.

elements.name: Brute Force (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Brute feature.

Starting at 3rd level, you’re able to strike with your weapons with especially brutal force. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Brutish Durability (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Brute feature.

Beginning at 7th level, your toughness allows you to shrug off assaults that would devastate others. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Additional Fighting Style (Brute UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Brute feature.

At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.

elements.name: Devastating Critical (UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Brute feature.

Starting at 15th level, when you score a critical hit with a weapon attack, you gain a bonus to that weapon’s damage roll equal to your level in this class.

elements.name: Survivor (Brute UA)
elements.desc:
18th-level Brute feature.

At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns in combat, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point). See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Bonus Proficiency (Cavalier UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Cavalier feature.

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, History, Insight, Performance, or Persuasion. Alternatively, you learn one language of your choice.

elements.name: Born to the Saddle (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Cavalier feature.

Starting at 3rd level, your mastery as a rider becomes apparent. You have advantage on saving throws made to avoid falling off your mount. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Unwavering Mark (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Cavalier feature.

At 3rd level, you gain a set of combat abilities, referred to as maneuvers, which are fueled by special dice called superiority dice. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Ferocious Charger (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Cavalier feature.

At 7th level, you gain additional benefits when you use your Trip Attack maneuver. You can expend up to two superiority dice on it, adding both dice to the damage roll. When you spend two dice in this way, the target has disadvantage on its Strength saving throw to avoid being knocked prone.

elements.name: Improved Combat Superiority (UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Cavalier feature.

At 10th level, your superiority dice turn into d10s. At 18th level, they turn into d12s.

elements.name: Relentless (UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Cavalier feature.

Starting at 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain one superiority die.

elements.id: Class Feature:Born to the Saddle (Knight UA)
elements.name: Born to the Saddle (Knight UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Knight feature.

Starting at 3rd level, mounting or dismounting a creature costs you only 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed. In addition, you have advantage on saving throws made to avoid falling off your mount. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Implacable Mark (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Knight feature.

At 3rd level, you excel at foiling attacks and protecting your allies by menacing your foes. When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, the target is marked by you until the end of your next turn. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Noble Cavalry (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Knight feature.

At 7th level, you gain proficiency in two of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, History, Insight, Persuasion, or Religion. Alternatively, you learn one language of your choice.

elements.name: Hold the Line (UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Knight feature.

At 10th level, you master the ability to harass and slow your enemies. As a reaction when a creature moves at least 1 foot within 5 feet of you, you can make one melee weapon attack against that creature. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Rapid Strike (Knight UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Knight feature.

Starting at 15th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you have advantage on a weapon attack against a target on your turn, you can forgo that advantage to immediately make an additional weapon attack against the same target as a bonus action.

elements.name: Defender's Blade (UA)
elements.desc:
18th-level Knight feature.

At 18th level, you respond to danger with extraordinary vigilance. You can use your reaction for an opportunity attack even if you have already expended your reaction this round, but not if you have already used your reaction this turn. In addition, you gain a +1 bonus to AC while wearing heavy armor.

elements.name: Bonus Proficiencies (Monster Hunter UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Monster Hunter feature.

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in two of the following skills of your choice: Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Nature, or Perception. You can gain proficiency with a tool of your choice in place of one skill choice.

elements.name: Combat Superiority (Monster Hunter UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Monster Hunter feature.

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain a set of abilities that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Hunter's Mysticism (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Monster Hunter feature.

At 3rd level, your study of the supernatural gives you a limited ability to use magic. You can cast Detect Magic as a ritual. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Monster Slayer (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Monster Hunter feature.

At 7th level, whenever you expend superiority dice to add to a damage roll, you can expend up to two dice instead of just one, adding both to the roll. Both dice are expended as normal. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.id: Class Feature:Improved Combat Superiority (Monster Hunter UA)
elements.name: Improved Combat Superiority (Monster Hunter UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Monster Hunter feature.

At 10th level, your superiority dice turn into d10s. At 18th level, they turn into d12s.

elements.name: Relentless (Monster Hunter UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Monster Hunter feature.

Starting at 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain one superiority die.

elements.name: Psionic Talent (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Psi Knight feature.

At 3rd level, you harbor a wellspring of psionic power within yourself, an energy that ebbs and flows as you channel it in various ways. This power is represented by your Psionic Talent die, the starting size of which is a d6. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Psi Replenishment (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Psi Knight feature.

Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can calm your mind for a moment and restore your Psionic Talent die to its starting size. You then can’t use Psi Replenishment again until you finish a long rest.

elements.name: Telekinetic Adept (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Psi Knight feature.

By the 7th level, you have mastered new ways to use your telekinesis: See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Psi-Enhanced Metabolism (UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Psi Knight feature.

Starting at 10th level, the psionic energy flowing through you has bolstered your mind and body. You have resistance to poison and psychic damage, and you are immune to the poisoned condition.

elements.name: Bulwark of Force (UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Psi Knight feature.

At 15th level, you can shield yourself and others with telekinetic force. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Telekinetic Master (UA)
elements.desc:
18th-level Psi Knight feature.

When you reach 18th level, your ability to move creatures and objects with your mind is matched by few. If your Psionic Talent die is available, you can cast the telekinesis spell, requiring no components. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Telekinetic Hand (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Psychic Warrior feature.

At 3rd level, you learn the Mage Hand cantrip. You can cast it without components, and you can make the spectral hand invisible. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

elements.name: Psionic Armament (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Psychic Warrior feature.

Starting at 3rd level, you can channel your psychic power to magically augment your prowess. When you finish a long rest, choose whether to augment your defenses or your strikes. The chosen benefit lasts until you finish a long rest. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Strength of Mind (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Psychic Warrior feature.

At 7th level, as a bonus action, you can telekinetically lash out at a creature you can see within 20 feet of you. The target must make a Strength saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency modifier + your Intelligence modifier. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Telekinetic Bulwark (UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Psychic Warrior feature.

At 10th level, when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your attacks to project a bastion of psionic power in a 10-foot radius around yourself. It lasts for 1 minute or until you're incapacitated. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Agonizing Strikes (UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Psychic Warrior feature.

Starting at 15th level, your attacks can channel psychic agony. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Psychic Dreadnought (UA)
elements.desc:
18th-level Psychic Warrior feature.

At 18th level, the power of your mind suffuses your entire being, making you a nigh-unstoppable force on the battlefield. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Bonus Proficiencies (Rune Knight UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Rune Knight feature.

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with smith’s tools, and you learn to speak, read, and write Giant.

elements.name: Rune Magic (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Rune Knight feature.

Starting at 3rd level, you learn how to use runes to enhance your gear. When you gain this feature, you learn how to inscribe two runes of your choice on weapons, armor, or shields (see “Rune Options”). See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Giant Might (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Rune Knight feature.

At 3rd level, you can imbue yourself with the might of giants. As a bonus action, you magically gain the following benefits, which last for 1 minute: See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Defensive Runes (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Rune Knight feature.

At 7th level, you learn to invoke your rune magic to protect your allies. When another creature you can see within 60 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant a bonus to the creature’s AC against that attack. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Great Stature (UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Rune Knight feature.

By 10th level the magic of your runes permanently alters you. When you gain this feature, roll 3d4. You grow a number of inches in height equal to the roll. Moreover, the extra damage you deal with your Giant Might feature increases to 1d8. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Rune Magic Mastery (UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Rune Knight feature.

At 15th level, you can invoke each rune you know from your Rune Magic feature twice, rather than once, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

In addition, you learn one new rune of your choice from the Rune Magic feature (for a total of five).

elements.id: Class Feature:Blessing of the All Father (UA)
elements.name: Blessing of the All Father (UA)
elements.desc:
18th-level Rune Knight feature.

At 18th level, you learn how to share your rune magic with your allies. When you use your Giant Might feature, you can choose one willing creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The chosen creature also gains the benefits of your Giant Might feature.

elements.name: Bonus Proficiency (Samurai UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Samurai feature.

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: History, Insight, Performance, or Persuasion. Alternatively, you learn one language of your choice.

elements.name: Fighting Spirit (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Samurai feature.

Starting at 3rd level, the might of your willpower can shield you and help you strike true. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Elegant Courtier (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Samurai feature.

Starting at 7th level, your discipline and attention to detail allow you to excel in social situations that require strict adherence to etiquette. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Tireless Spirit (UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Samurai feature.

At 10th level, your superior willpower allows you to shrug off mind-assaulting effects. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma saving throws (choose one).

elements.name: Rapid Strike (Samurai UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Samurai feature.

Starting at 15th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you have advantage on a weapon attack against a target on your turn, you can forgo that advantage to immediately make an additional weapon attack against the same target as a bonus action.

elements.name: Strength Before Death (UA)
elements.desc:
18th-level Samurai feature.

Starting at 18th level, your fighting spirit can delay the grasp of death. If you take damage that would reduce you to 0 hit points, you can delay that damage and immediately take a bonus turn, interrupting the current turn. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Bonus Proficiencies (Scout UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Scout feature.

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in three of the following skills of your choice: Acrobatics, Athletics, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Stealth, or Survival. You can choose to gain proficiency with thieves’ tools in place of one skill choice.

elements.name: Combat Superiority (Scout UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Scout feature.

At 3rd level, you gain a set of abilities that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Natural Explorer (Scout UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Scout feature.

At 3rd level, you are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Improved Combat Superiority (Scout UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Scout feature.

At 10th level, your superiority dice turn into d10s. At 18th level, they turn into d12s.

elements.name: Relentless (Scout UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Scout feature.

Starting at 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain 1 superiority die.

elements.name: Steady Aim (UA)
elements.desc:
3rd-level Sharpshooter feature.

Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your aim becomes deadly. As a bonus action on your turn, you can take careful aim at a creature you can see that is within range of a ranged weapon you’re wielding. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Careful Eyes (UA)
elements.desc:
7th-level Sharpshooter feature.

Starting at 7th level, you excel at picking out hidden enemies and other threats. You can take the Search action as a bonus action.

You also gain proficiency in the Perception, Investigation, or Survival skill (choose one).

elements.name: Close-Quarters Shooting (UA)
elements.desc:
10th-level Sharpshooter feature.

At 10th level, you learn to handle yourself in close combat. Making a ranged attack roll while within 5 feet of an enemy doesn’t impose disadvantage on your roll. See the side panel for the full text.

elements.name: Rapid Strike (Sharpshooter UA)
elements.desc:
15th-level Sharpshooter feature.

Starting at 15th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you have advantage on a weapon attack against a target on your turn, you can forgo that advantage to immediately make an additional weapon attack against the same target as a bonus action.

elements.name: Snap Shot (UA)
elements.desc:
18th-level Sharpshooter feature.

Starting at 18th level, you are ever ready to spring into action. If you take the Attack action on your first turn of a combat, you can make one additional ranged weapon attack as part of that action.
